findings.issue_text: Aggregate verdict: **NEEDS_REVISION**. Duplicate reports from multiple lenses are merged below.
No findings; all four deterministic reviewers returned PASS (`PASS_ADVISORY`).

`docs/tasks/task-001.md:1` — Blocking: the task has no acceptance criteria defining supported apps, sync contracts, user/team behavior, webhook semantics, error handling, or verification requirements.
No test/spec files or validation evidence cover the new webhook and enabled/disabled refresh paths, provider fallbacks, team credentials, malformed input, or persistence.
`packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96` — Critical: `prisma.credential.update()` is called without importing or defining `prisma`, causing type-check/runtime failure.

`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:40` — High: `appStoreMetadata` is indexed using the public slug although its keys are directory names; valid apps such as `google-calendar`, `lark-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, and `msteams` can incorrectly return 404.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8` — High: sync mode returns a Fetch `Response`, but Google reads `.data` and HubSpot treats it as a `HubspotToken`, yielding undefined tokens and invalid expiry values.

`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97` — High: Google persists the complete Zod `{success,data}` result as `credential.key`; the next credential-schema parse rejects the wrapper. This also breaks ordinary non-sync refreshes.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:6` — High: the documented “access token and expiry” response contract cannot satisfy Lark’s nested refresh response or Webex’s required scope, token type, refresh token, and expiry fields.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5` — High: computed keys built from `z.string().toString()` become literal object keys rather than catch-all validators, so genuine expiry and provider fields are stripped.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25` — High: missing refresh tokens are replaced with the literal `"refresh_token"`; Office 365 can persist that unusable token while retaining an already-expired expiry value.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15` — High: parser selection uses only global sharing configuration, while refresh delegation additionally requires `userId`; team credentials and direct Salesforce refreshes are consequently parsed using the wrong schema.
`packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75` — High: Salesforce bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so configuring the credential-sync endpoint does not enable Salesforce syncing.
`packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:101` — High: after persisting the refreshed Salesforce token, the current connection is constructed with the stale pre-refresh access token.
`packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:55` — Medium: every service construction performs an unconditional Salesforce refresh and database write without checking expiry.
`packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86` — Medium: success is tested with `response.statusText === "OK"`; valid 2xx responses with an empty or different reason phrase are rejected.

`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31` — Medium: schema parsing, decryption, and `JSON.parse` errors are uncaught, turning malformed requests or configuration into undefined 500 responses rather than controlled 4xx errors.

`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62` — High: synchronization identifies credentials only by `(userId, appSlug)` and updates an arbitrary `findFirst` result, so users with multiple accounts for one app can have the wrong credential overwritten.

`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62` — High: the check-then-create flow has no transaction, unique selector, or idempotency key; concurrent first deliveries can create duplicates and make later updates nondeterministic.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:42` — Medium: OAuth installation unnecessarily materializes every team member even though the membership predicate already establishes access.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:9` — High: OAuth state is parsed and reserialized without unpredictability, integrity protection, or session binding, enabling login-CSRF/account-linking attacks across the migrated OAuth flows.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:35` — High: the team branch permits any accepted member to create team-scoped credentials and bypasses the imported administrator-access guard.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8` — High: outbound credential-sync requests contain only numeric user ID and app slug, with no secret or signature; a reachable sync endpoint cannot authenticate Cal.com without undeclared out-of-band controls.
No findings; the diff remains traceable to the broad OAuth credential-sync/app-integration intent.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

In LarkCalendarService, the response goes through handleLarkError which expects a specific nested structure. If the external endpoint returns a flat structure but Lark expects nested data, this could be a real issue. However, this is a design choice for self-hosters implementing their own credential sync - they need to return the appropriate format. The finding has merit but is speculative about what the external endpoint returns.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, the function checks `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` to decide which schema to use. However, in refreshOAuthTokens.ts, the condition is `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`. This is a real inconsistency - the parser selection doesn't account for the userId condition that determines whether external refresh was actually used. For team credentials or when userId is null, the wrong schema could be applied.

This is a real correctness issue - the webhook provides no way to identify which specific credential should be updated when a user has multiple credentials for the same app. The schema only includes userId, appSlug, and keys - no credential identifier.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62` — High: the check-then-create flow has no transaction, unique selector, or idempotency key; concurrent first deliveries can create duplicates and make later updates nondeterministic.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts lines 57-91, there's a findFirst followed by either update or create without any transaction or unique constraint handling. The flow is: 1) findFirst to check if credential exists, 2) if exists, update it, 3) if not exists, create it. Between the findFirst and create, another concurrent request could also find no existing credential and both would attempt to create, resulting in duplicate credentials for the same userId+appId combination. This is a real race condition that could cause data integrity issues in a webhook endpoint that might receive concurrent requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8` — High: outbound credential-sync requests contain only numeric user ID and app slug, with no secret or signature; a reachable sync endpoint cannot authenticate Cal.com without undeclared out-of-band controls.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the refreshOAuthTokens function in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, it makes a POST request with only calcomUserId and appSlug in the body. There is no authentication header, secret, or signature included in this outbound request. The comment says 'Customize the payload based on what your endpoint requires' but the actual implementation sends no authentication. This is a legitimate security concern - the external endpoint receiving these requests has no way to verify they're coming from a legitimate Cal.com instance. While the inbound webhook (app-credential.ts) does verify CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, the outbound requests in refreshOAuthTokens have no such protection.
